rounds.text: Worth Peripherals Ltd trades at an attractive valuation discount, with a P/E of 14.6x against a sector benchmark of 21.73x and an EV/EBITDA of 7.94x compared to its sector benchmark of 12.1x [E6, E11]. The underlying balance sheet is conservatively managed, featuring a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x as of September 2026 and a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 2.84x [E34, E35]. Operational efficiency is improving, evidenced by working capital requirements dropping significantly from 51.0 days to 36.0 days and operating cash flow reaching Rs 30 Cr in March 2026 with a robust cash conversion of 1.58x [E31, E32, E55]. Furthermore, capital expenditure is largely completed with CWIP standing at Rs 0 Cr, indicating that new capacity is coming online, while the company operates against a supportive macro backdrop with the Capital Goods sector in a clear tailwind [E37, E68, E69]. Conceded: the company has delivered poor sales growth of 7.07% over the past five years alongside declining compounded profit growth of -30% in the trailing twelve months, reflecting near-term earnings pressure [E19, E56]. Conceded: promoter holding has decreased by 6.08 percentage points over the last three years down to 68.22%, and free cash flow was negative at Rs -52 Cr in March 2026 [E33, E38, E60].

The fundamental engine of Worth Peripherals Ltd is severely sputtering, evidenced by a dramatic contraction in profitability featuring a 30% drop in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a -7% decline over 3 years [E18, E19]. This earnings decay is highlighted by a sharp quarterly collapse where operating margins dropped by 4 percentage points to 7% in September 2026 compared to the prior year, alongside a net profit plunge of 64% year-over-year [E28, E66]. Valuation metrics fail to provide any cushion for these deteriorating fundamentals, as a discounted cash flow model yields an intrinsic value of Rs 139 against a market price of Rs 147, creating a negative margin of safety of -5.9% [E41, E42]. Furthermore, capital allocation and financial health show glaring cracks, most notably demonstrated by a severe free cash flow burn of Rs -52 crore in March 2026, an increase in borrowings to Rs 54 crore, and a steady erosion of promoter stake by 6.08 percentage points since December 2023 [E33, E36, E38]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x and a comfortable current ratio of 2.84x, indicating solid short-term liquidity [E34, E35]. However, this sturdy balance sheet does not excuse stagnant long-term top-line growth of just 1% over 3 years and 7% over 5 years, which severely lags behind the broader sector median sales growth of 22.2% [E14, E15, E71].

Conceded: compounded profit growth stands at -7% over 3 years and -30% over the trailing twelve months, alongside a -64% net profit drop year-over-year [E18, E19, E66]. However, the bear overstates the margin contraction narrative by ignoring that the TTM operating margin actually expanded by 1 percentage point to 10% compared to three years earlier [E27]. The severe free cash flow burn of ₹ -52 Cr in March 2026 is fully contextualized by capital expenditure completion, evidenced by Capital Work-in-Progress dropping 100% to ₹ 0 Cr by September 2026, meaning new capacity is now coming online [E33, E37]. Conceded: intrinsic value sits slightly below market price at ₹ 139 [E41]. Yet the bear's valuation panic ignores that the stock trades at a P/E of 14.6x against a sector benchmark of 21.73x and an EV/EBITDA of 7.94x against a sector benchmark of 12.1x, representing a clear relative discount [E6, E11]. Furthermore, top-line deceleration is balanced by a recent acceleration to 10% sales growth over the trailing twelve months, supported by a constructive capital goods sector tailwind score of +0.57 [E16, E68].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 14.6x against a sector benchmark of 21.73x and an EV/EBITDA of 7.94x against a sector benchmark of 12.1x [E6, E11]. However, this relative discount is fully justified by fundamental underperformance, as the bull attempts to minimize a severe -30% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a -64% net profit drop year-over-year [E19, E66]. While the bull points to a 1 percentage point expansion in TTM operating margins, it completely ignores the alarming quarterly collapse to 7% in September 2026—a steep 4 percentage point drop from the year-ago quarter—alongside an inconsistent margin trend [E27, E28, E30]. The bull's dismissal of the ₹ -52 Cr free cash flow burn as mere capex completion glosses over the fact that borrowings simultaneously surged to ₹ 54 Cr from ₹ 42 Cr, while promoter holdings actively diluted by 6.08 percentage points [E33, E36, E38, E37]. Finally, the cited capital goods sector tailwind of +0.57 rings hollow when the company's own sales growth is lagging far behind sector median growth rates of 22.2% [E16, E68, E70, E71].
